claims.text: Laser cladding can produce eutectic or hypereutectic CoCrFeNiMo high-entropy-alloy coatings.
The proposed coating has an FCC matrix containing dispersed σ or related hard second phases.
The σ phase is hard and electrochemically dissimilar from the FCC phase.
Potential differences between the FCC and σ phases cause galvanic corrosion.
An oxide film forms on the coating surface during friction and wear.
At elevated temperature, a protective oxide film is cyclically ruptured by mechanical stress.
Rupture of the oxide film produces adhesive and abrasive wear.
Galvanic corrosion and mechanically induced oxide-film rupture act synergistically to accelerate overall degradation.
Changing laser-cladding conditions or post-processing can provide a multiphase coating and a compositionally matched, near-single-phase coating for comparison.
A homogeneous, predominantly single-phase coating has minimal internal electrochemical-potential differences.
The relevant test condition is simultaneous sliding or abrasive wear and corrosion at about 600 °C in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution.
Interfaces between electrochemically dissimilar phases are sites of local galvanic coupling.
The same phase interfaces are preferential sites for oxide-film rupture.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the multiphase coating will exhibit higher total degradation.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the multiphase coating will exhibit a higher wear rate because of more frequent oxide-film rupture and abrasive wear.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the multiphase coating will exhibit a higher corrosion-current density because of intensified galvanic effects.
The hypothesis applies when sustained contact stress and corrosive attack coincide at temperatures where oxide films form and are repeatedly removed.
Phase separation must occur at a microstructural scale sufficient to establish local galvanic cells.
Wear volume, coefficient of friction, corrosion-current density, and post-test microstructure can be measured in the controlled comparison.
Failure of the multiphase coating to show significantly higher wear and corrosion-current density than the homogeneous baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
